issues.summary: The fix has no component regression test; nothing in unit tests would catch a revert from useWatch back to watch()
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: The only colocated test in apps/mobile/src/components/SafeAccountInput is hooks/useImportSafe.test.tsx, and it covers the hook, not whether SafeAccountInput re-renders. The success icon is only asserted in Maestro flows (apps/mobile/e2e/tests/onboarding/add-existing-safe.yml and others), which do not run by default on PRs. React Compiler is enabled only through app.config.ts:219 experiments. Because of that, a plain Jest render test might pass with either API. I could not confirm this without node_modules, but it makes a missed regression more likely, not less.

issues.summary: useImportSafe reads safeAddress with watch() in the same child, so under React Compiler memoisation the debounced lookup may keep a stale address
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: useImportSafe.ts:31 uses watch('safeAddress') inside SafeAccountInput. Under React Compiler (app.config.ts:219), SafeAccountInput takes no props and is rendered inside ImportAccountFormView at line 64, so a root re-render only reaches it if context or props change. Pasting one valid address over another leaves isEnteredAddressValid and errors unchanged, so a stale value is plausible. This is the same mechanism the PR describes, but the line is outside the PR's diff and I have not confirmed it at runtime.

issues.summary: The address is cast to `0x${string}` for Identicon without checking that it is hex
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: index.tsx:37 was not changed by this PR. The cast is only a type assertion, and nobody showed that Identicon misbehaves when given a non-hex string, so there is no demonstrated cost.

issues.summary: The new useWatch comment is inconsistent with the uncommented useWatch in ImportAccountFormView
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: index.tsx:19-20 adds a two-line comment explaining why useWatch is used instead of watch(). This is a matter of style. The comment arguably helps, because it explains a non-obvious subscription detail that stops someone from 'simplifying' the code back to watch().

issues.summary: The useWatch comment could be shorter
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: index.tsx:19-20 is two short lines that are already accurate. Rewording them is a preference with no concrete cost.
